stem:
A microphone is connected to a cathode ray oscilloscope. A loudspeaker giving a single note is switched on. The trace shown in the figure appears on the screen.

(The given trace is a smooth sine wave of amplitude 2 m showing two complete cycles.)

Which of the following shows the softer but same-frequency note of the given note?
(a) A sine wave of amplitude 2 m with three complete cycles (same loudness, higher frequency)
(b) A sine wave of amplitude 1 m with two complete cycles (smaller amplitude, same number of cycles)
(c) A sine wave of amplitude 1 m with three complete cycles (smaller amplitude, higher frequency)
(d) A sine wave of amplitude 2 m with two complete cycles (same as the given trace)

A student plotted the following four graphs representing the variation of velocity \(v\) of sound in a gas with the pressure \(P\) for a given temperature. Which one is correct?
(a) A horizontal straight line (\(v\) stays constant as \(P\) increases)
(b) A curve that decreases as \(P\) increases (\(v\) falls with \(P\))
(c) A straight line through the origin sloping upward (\(v\) directly proportional to \(P\))
(d) A rising curve that flattens off (\(v\) increases then levels with \(P\))

The following figure shows the displacement-time graph for a sound wave produced by an instrument.

(The given graph is a smooth sine wave of amplitude 5 cm and period 6 s, with zero crossings at 3 s, 6 s and 9 s.)

Which graph can be obtained when another musical instrument produces a note of the same pitch but of a different quality?
(a) A smooth sine wave of amplitude 5 cm and period 4 s (higher frequency)
(b) A complex (distorted, flat-topped) wave of amplitude 5 cm and period 6 s (same period, different waveform shape)
(c) A smooth sine wave of amplitude 5 cm and period 6 s (identical to the given wave)
(d) A wave of small amplitude (about 2 cm) with low rounded humps

The diagram represents two different sound waves, Wave X and Wave Y.

(Wave X is a large-amplitude sine wave of period \(T\). Wave Y is a smaller-amplitude sine wave of period \(T/2\), so Wave Y completes its cycles in half the time of Wave X.)

Choose the correct statement.

options.label: A
options.text: The frequency of X is less than Y but its pitch is same as Y.

options.label: B
options.text: The frequency and pitch of X is same as the frequency and pitch of Y.

options.label: C
options.text: The frequency and pitch of X is less than that of Y.

options.label: D
options.text: The frequency of X is same as Y but its pitch is higher than Y.

stem:
The wave having an amplitude of 5 cm and frequency \(f = 100\ 	ext{Hz}\) can be best represented by:
(a) A sine wave that starts by dipping negative first, with no marked amplitude or period values
(b) A positive-going sine wave of amplitude 5 cm completing one full cycle in 0.01 s (zero crossing at 0.005 s, cycle ending at 0.01 s)
(c) A triangular wave of amplitude 5 cm and period 0.01 s
(d) A sine wave with amplitude/period values that do not match 5 cm and 0.01 s
